description: Default first step for research: one search over papers, books, patents, standards, Wikipedia articles and YouTube transcripts, and public discussion on Reddit, Telegram and Discord, plus relevant web pages, for literature reviews, fact-checking, prior art, current events and first-hand experience. Returns compact ranked hits with their source, a canonical source_uri, one matching snippet, an abstract preview, authors, date, and estimated full-text size. Narrow with types and publication dates. Snippet offsets use Unicode characters in the stored source field; null truncation flags mean unknown, never false. Use varied focused queries; fetch only the strongest hits.

issued_after.description: Only results published at or after this Unix timestamp (seconds, UTC, inclusive); use this argument instead of after: in query. Any date bound excludes undated documents.

issued_before.description: Only results published at or before this Unix timestamp (seconds, UTC, inclusive); use this argument instead of before: in query. Must not be earlier than issued_after.

limit.description: Results to return. Keep 10 for normal agent use; use 5 when issuing several parallel queries.

offset.description: Use next_offset from a prior result with the same query and filters; offset + limit must not exceed 500.

query.description: Focused natural-language or keyword query. There is no two-word query or phrase limit. Preserve complete concepts and relationships; use full natural-language questions when useful. Quote established phrases whose wording must appear, including three-to-eight-word technical terms or longer known titles. Example: "long term exposure to air pollution" respiratory morbidity and mortality. Leave uncertain wording unquoted. For claim verification, search the relationship rather than requiring the entire statement verbatim. Every quoted span is required; multiple spans mean ALL, not alternatives. Matching uses ordered normalized indexed tokens, not byte-exact text; straight, curly, and guillemet quote pairs work. If results are sparse, relax optional phrases and explain the broader search; preserve wording the user explicitly requires. Boolean and field operators are not supported. May be empty only with a date filter.

types.description: Result types to include; omit for all. web: web pages (needs a query; accounts that have paid); science: articles, proceedings, preprints, dissertations and reports; books: books and chapters; science and books together cover the whole library, including patents, standards and Wikipedia; social: Reddit, Telegram and Discord posts. Date filters apply to every type.

name: machinelibrary_search

hint.description: Why a search found nothing and how to rephrase; null when there are hits.

feedback_eligible.description: Whether this response supplies a feedback receipt covering this result. False for external web results or missing receipts (including citation backlinks). Omit false results from ratings and receipt-bound search_result context.

id.description: Returned document ID. Copy into feedback document_id only when feedback_eligible is true.

issued_at.description: Publication time, Unix seconds; null when unknown.

issued_at_datetime.description: issued_at as RFC 3339 UTC (2026-07-12T10:00:00Z); null when unknown.

snippet.description: Best query-matching excerpt, capped at 900 characters.

snippet_end_char.description: Exclusive Unicode scalar end offset in the full snippet_field; null when unknown.

snippet_start_char.description: Zero-based Unicode scalar offset in the original stored snippet_field (including content). Null means unknown, not zero.

snippet_table_header.description: When the excerpt continues a Markdown table, that table's caption, header and separator rows, which name its columns. Context only: not part of the excerpt or its offsets.

snippet_truncated_end.description: True: source text follows the excerpt. False: verified end of the field. Null: unknown (legacy or redacted source), NEVER equivalent to false.

snippet_truncated_start.description: True: source text precedes the excerpt. False: verified start of the field. Null: unknown (legacy or redacted source), NEVER equivalent to false. Whole sentences may be omitted; fetch context before resolving dangling references.

source.description: documents (papers, books, patents, standards, Wikipedia, YouTube transcripts), social (Reddit, Telegram, Discord) or web.

source_uri.description: Canonical URI to copy verbatim into fetch tools and citations. Null for records stored without any identifier: read them by passing search_result and cite them by title.

next_offset.description: Pass as offset to retrieve the next page.

feedback_token.description: Receipt for feedback and attributing document reads. Copy only into search_result or the feedback tool; never include it in answers or citations.
